plan.contextChunk: This figure combines a ray construction with an intensity curve for light passing through a single slit. At the left a vertical tan barrier is drawn in two segments with a narrow gap between them; a double-headed arrow spans the gap and a curved arrow connects it to the label a. A short teal arrow labeled lambda enters horizontally from the left and reaches the opening. From the slit five gray dashed lines fan out to the right toward a vertical gray line labeled Screen, and the middle dashed line runs straight along the horizontal. Two arcs measure angles from that horizontal reference: the outer upper line is marked theta_2 = 45 degrees and the inner upper line is marked theta_1 = ?, with two more dashed lines mirroring them below the axis. Drawn on the screen is a red wavy curve, tied by a curved arrow to the label Intensity on screen, whose sideways excursion represents brightness; it has a tall broad central peak on the axis and smaller lobes above and below, and each dashed ray meets the screen exactly where the curve pinches in to nothing. Lining the ray directions up with the nulls of the curve identifies each dashed line with a numbered diffraction minimum, so that the known 45 degree direction can be used to recover the slit width a and then the unknown angle theta_1.

interactionPlan.concept: In single-slit diffraction, the dark fringes occur at directions satisfying a sin(θ) = mλ, so increasing wavelength spreads the minima outward while increasing slit width pulls them inward.

interactions.label: Slit width a
interactions.teaches: Wider slits make the diffraction minima occur at smaller angles, so the screen pattern compresses toward the central axis

interactions.label: Wavelength λ
interactions.teaches: Longer wavelengths make the minima occur at larger angles, so the side lobes and zero-intensity points spread farther from the center
Each dashed ray direction corresponds to a zero of the intensity curve, and selecting a minimum links its angle θ to the integer order m in a sin(θ) = mλ

demo_steps.title: Identify the minima
demo_steps.narration: The dashed construction rays are not brightness peaks; they mark the directions where the single-slit intensity falls to zero. Click θ1, θ2, or a mirrored minimum to see the ray and its zero-intensity pinch point highlight together.

demo_steps.title: Use the known 45° minimum
demo_steps.narration: With θ2 fixed at 45°, the second minimum satisfies a sin(45°) = 2λ. This determines the slit width in wavelength units, which can then be used to predict the unknown first-minimum angle θ1.

demo_steps.title: Make the slit wider
demo_steps.narration: Increasing a while λ stays fixed pulls the dashed minimum rays closer to the central line and narrows the diffraction pattern on the screen.

demo_steps.title: Use longer wavelength light
demo_steps.narration: Increasing λ while a stays fixed pushes the minimum directions outward and widens the red intensity pattern, making the dependence on the ratio λ/a visible.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The geometry rays and the red intensity curve are two views of the same condition: every diffraction minimum occurs where a sin(θ) equals an integer number of wavelengths.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Recreate the original as a left-to-right optics diagram. Put the tan slit barrier on the left, the gray screen line on the right, and the slit opening as the common origin of five dashed gray rays: central horizontal, ±first minimum, and ±second minimum. Draw θ1 as the smaller upper angle and θ2 = 45° as the larger upper angle. The red curve should run vertically along the screen while bulging sideways to show intensity: largest central lobe on the horizontal axis, smaller lobes above and below, and exact zeros aligned with the noncentral dashed rays. Slider changes should recompute minima using a sin(θ) = mλ and redraw both dashed rays and red sinc-squared intensity nulls consistently; if a selected order is no longer physically allowed, fade that ray and label rather than drawing an impossible angle.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for slit width a: learner changes the opening while lambda stays fixed; the dashed minimum directions and red intensity nulls spread apart or compress; the inverse relationship between slit width and diffraction-pattern angular spacing becomes clear.
- Slider for wavelength lambda: learner changes the incoming wavelength; the intensity lobes and minimum angles shift outward for longer wavelengths and inward for shorter ones; the condition a sin(theta)=m lambda becomes visible on the screen.
- Click on a diffraction minimum: learner selects theta_1, theta_2, or its mirrored counterpart; the corresponding dashed ray and zero-intensity pinch point highlight together; the alignment between geometric angles and zeros of the intensity curve becomes clear.

authoredContext:
Calculating Single-Slit Diffraction Visible light of wavelength 550 nm falls on a single slit and produces its second diffraction minimum at an angle of 45.0° relative to the incident direction of the light, as in the figure. (a) What is the width of the slit? (b) At what angle is the first minimum produced?

In this example, we analyze a graph of the single-slit diffraction pattern.

Figure shows a vertical line on the left. This has a slit in the middle, of length a. A ray labeled lambda passes horizontally through the slit. This splits into 5 dotted lines that fall on a screen. The screen is shown as a vertical line. Of the five dotted lines, two make angles theta 1 and theta 2 with the horizontal. Theta 2 is 45 degrees. Theta 1 is smaller than theta 2 and is unknown. Intensity on the screen is shown as a vertical wave. The crest at the center, where a horizontal dotted line from the center of the slit falls on the screen, is the largest. The wave attenuates at the top and bottom. The remaining four dotted lines correspond to troughs in the wave.

Strategy From the given information, and assuming the screen is far away from the slit, we can use the equation asinθ=mλ first to find D, and again to find the angle for the first minimum θ1.

discrepancies: the generated figure adds hollow red circular markers at the screen intersections of the dashed rays, which are not present in the source static figure and make the construction look more annotated than the original
the bottom label is clipped: the source clearly reads “Intensity on screen,” but the generated default view only shows “Intensity” because “on screen” is placed below the visible SVG area
the intensity-arrow annotation is shifted too low compared with the source, contributing to the clipped label and reducing resemblance at the bottom right
the red intensity curve is slightly simplified/truncated near the bottom compared with the source, where the lower oscillation and label region remain fully visible
evaluation.notes: The generated figure is clearly recognizable and conceptually correct, with strong interactive controls, but it adds non-source zero markers and clips the important “on screen” portion of the intensity label.
action_items: Move the “Intensity on screen” label and curved arrow upward so both label lines are fully visible inside the SVG viewbox.
Remove or hide the hollow red zero-intensity circles in the default static state, or only show them after user interaction so the initial view matches the source.
Extend or reposition the lower part of the red intensity curve so the bottom oscillation and screen annotation resemble the source more closely.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interactivity are correct, but the remaining problems are concrete rendering fixes: clipped label placement, extra non-source markers, and minor curve positioning.

discrepancies: The red intensity curve is much closer to a nearly vertical line outside the central lobe; the source shows visibly larger wavy side lobes above and below the main maximum.
The 'Screen' label is offset to the left of the vertical screen line rather than centered above it as in the source.
The slit-width/aperture annotation on the left is slightly mis-scaled: the curly brace and vertical double arrow are more separated and less like the compact source annotation.
The generated slit point includes a visible dark dot at the aperture, whereas the source primarily uses the ray convergence point without emphasizing a filled dot.
evaluation.notes: The generated figure is clearly recognizable and conceptually correct, with strong interactions, but the intensity-profile shape and a few annotation placements are less faithful to the source.
action_items: Increase or visually exaggerate the red intensity side lobes so the profile more closely matches the source illustration rather than appearing almost flat outside the central maximum.
Center the 'Screen' label directly above the vertical screen line.
Tighten and rescale the left aperture annotation so the curly brace, vertical double arrow, and 'a' label match the compact layout of the source.
De-emphasize or remove the filled dot at the slit if aiming for a closer static replacement.
